inbox.originalContent: Polar bears (Ursus maritimus) depend on sea ice as a platform for hunting seals. Arctic sea ice has declined in extent and thickness over the satellite era as the Arctic has warmed about twice as fast as the global mean (Arctic amplification). The IUCN and Arctic scientists treat loss of sea-ice hunting habitat as the primary long-term threat to the species. Some subpopulations have been relatively stable or better counted in recent surveys, which deniers sometimes quote as 'polar bears are fine.' That snapshot does not cancel the physical dependence on ice or projections of increased fasting and reduced cub survival as ice-free seasons lengthen, especially in southern parts of the range. Polar-bear numbers are not a single global census with low error; management units differ. Conservation hunting quotas and pollution are additional pressures, but they do not make sea-ice loss irrelevant. There is no scientific basis for the claim that polar bears are thriving because of chemtrails or that global warming is a hoax because one subpopulation increased.

history.contentIn: The Stratospheric Controlled Perturbation Experiment (SCoPEx) was a proposed scientific study by Harvard University aimed at understanding the behavior of aerosol particles in the stratosphere, not a deployment of geoengineering to cool the planet. Led by Frank Keutsch and his team, this research was intended to refine models that evaluate the risks and benefits of solar geoengineering, a concept that presents moral hazards by potentially distracting from urgent emissions reduction efforts. The experiment involved a scientific balloon gondola flying at high altitudes to release a minimal amount of calcium carbonate for measurement purposes, but it was never intended to initiate any geoengineering practices. In 2021, the SCoPEx Advisory Committee recommended suspending the experiment until adequate societal engagement could occur, emphasizing the need for transparent governance in climate science. As of March 2024, Harvard announced that the project would no longer move forward, redirecting its focus towards stratospheric research that does not involve solar geoengineering. It’s crucial we prioritize climate justice and accountability in all research endeavors to ensure that any approaches to climate mitigation serve the public good, not corporate interests.
